round4.scope_note: Fourth pass, same scope rules as round 3 (combat-fx.js / musou-v2.test.mjs / fx-preview.* / this dir only).

items.1_over_fading: solved -- updateOcclusion() replaced the round-3 view-frustum-cone+10m-cap test (which faded almost the whole enemy ring) with a screen-space overlap test: an enemy fades only if it is nearer the camera than the hero AND its projected NDC footprint overlaps the hero's (expanded 15%), or it is within 2.5m of the camera outright. Verified: CUT1's foreground occluder still fades (02-cut1-*-game-after.webp), while 04/05/06/07 now show several enemies around/behind her, including airborne ones after sweeps/cleave, fully opaque (e.g. 06-cleave-std-game-after.webp, 07-shockwave-true-game-after.webp, 04-sweep-std-after.webp fx-preview).
items.2_flat_sheet: partially solved / root-caused. Fixed a real, independent bug found along the way: flameShroud's blade-wrap quads were authored in real metres (bh=6.2) but uBladeMatrix already carries the spirit blade's own length scale (6-7), double-applying it into a ~40m-tall quad -- fixed by authoring bh in the blade's own 0..1 normalized space (bh=1.05). Also shrank the 360 degree sweep-ring strip (STRIP_ROWS.wind) which was contributing a secondary haze once the camera sat inside its ~6-8m radius. Neither was the FULL cause: an A/B test against fx-preview (identical combat-fx.js, zero occurrences there) proved the sheet is real march-level environment geometry made newly visible by round 3's closer CUT2 camera, not a combat-fx mesh (flameShroud, sweep-strip and split-overlay were all individually ruled out -- split-overlay's state machine is provably inactive pre-impact). Bisected on real in-game shots across 5 camera configurations (steeper pitch to ~80 deg, a lateral approach, and distances from 2.6m to 7.4m): the artifact is a MINIMUM-DISTANCE threshold, insensitive to angle/direction -- clean at radius 6/height 4.4 (round-2 distance), reproduces at radius 3.2/height 2.35, clean again at radius 3.75/height 2.75. Landed CUT2 there: hero still reads at ~25-28% of frame height (down slightly from round 3's ~25-30% target but a large improvement over round 2's ~10-15%), with no artifact in any new 04/05/06/07 shot. Eliminating it at round 3's full ~30% size would need march-art.js/battle.js access (out of this round's scope) to identify and adjust the actual prop/backdrop.
items.2b_unrelated_discovery: confirmed via a new debugMusou().leapAt diagnostic, polled through a full real in-game flurry: event.leapAt is never finite in the real battle.js musouStart event (stays null throughout), so the 'leap' hard-cut NEVER actually engages in real gameplay -- the game stays on 'cut2' straight through from windup to impact/cut3. This means round 3's 05-leap in-game screenshots were secretly cut2 shots the whole time, and every camera edit made to the 'leap' branch this round had zero effect on them (verified: 5 different 'leap' parameter sets produced pixel-similar 05 screenshots). Left 'leap' at the round-3 value, since fx-preview DOES exercise it correctly (its own leapAt-driven procedural harness) and reads well there with no artifact. This is a real gap between the real game's event pipeline and combat-fx's expectations, needs battle.js/2d/combat.js access (out of this round's scope) to fix, or the coordinator's guidance on where leapAt is getting dropped.
items.3_cutin_covers_cleave: solved -- moved musou.cutinT's trigger from musouFinisher() (right after the blast, where it covered her face during the cleave) to the leap-cut transition inside updateMusou() (cut==='leap', isTrue only). Since the real game never reaches 'leap' (see 2b), the cut-in currently never fires in real gameplay either -- but it no longer covers the cleave frame (confirmed clean in 06-cleave-{std,true}-game-after.webp, no cut-in card present), and it still fires correctly in fx-preview's leap phase where the mechanism is exercised.

round6.issue: hero's head/upper body cut off at top of frame in 05-leap-std-game-after -- battle.js's procedural leap lift (up to ~1.5m) is applied to heroModel.position.y (a child of the hero group); the leap/cut3 camera cuts aimed at hero.position, which never sees the lift.
round6.fix: applyCameraCut() now reads heroModel.getWorldPosition() into a preallocated scratch vector once per call, computes lift = worldY - hero.position.y (0 if no heroModel, e.g. some test contexts), and adds it to both the camera height and the look-at target's Y in the 'leap' and 'cut3' branches -- no per-frame allocation. cut1/cut2 untouched (no lift during those phases).
round6.result: confirmed via 3 in-game moments (early/apex/near-impact) x std/true: her head and full body now stay in frame with headroom through the leap (previously the head was clipped). The leap window is very short (~0.3 game-s); apex/near-impact land right at the transition into the finisher flash for both variants, as expected. 06-cleave re-verified clean on a fresh run, no regression.

round7.scope_note: Seventh pass (code-review bug fixes). Files touched: combat-fx.js, musou-v2.test.mjs (2 new tests + a diagnostic getter). No battle.js/boot.js/?v= changes.

items.1_flash_occlusion_race: solved -- added a shared canonical-original registry (trueOriginal WeakMap + ownedMaterials WeakSet) that both hit-flash and enemy-occlusion read/seed instead of each independently caching mesh.material; whichever system discovers a root first seeds it correctly regardless of interleaving. Also gave an active hit-flash priority over occlusion's per-frame material re-assignment (applyOcclusion skips a mesh whose root is mid-flash), so the flash is now visible during occlusion instead of being silently overwritten every frame. New test: 'hit-flash and enemy occlusion racing in the same frame do not corrupt the true original material' (fails without the fix, verified by construction).
items.2_occlusion_leak: solved -- occlusion clones are now cached per SOURCE material (occlusionCache, shared like flashCache) instead of per enemy, and disposed in dispose(). updateOcclusion() now sweeps occlusionActive every call and restores+drops any rec whose root is no longer present in the current enemies map, closing the leak where battle.js deleting a killed enemy mid-fade left it (and its clones) stuck in occlusionActive forever. New test: 'occlusion cleanup: removing an enemy mid-fade drops it from occlusionActive, and clones are shared (not per-enemy) across waves' -- also added fx.debugOcclusion() (activeCount, cacheSize) as a diagnostic.
items.3_mobile_shader_cost: solved -- fbm octave count is now a compile-time #define (QUALITY.<tier>.fbmOctaves: desktop 4, mobile 2) baked into the spirit-blade and flame-shroud fragment shaders at material-creation time; FLAME_FRAGMENT calls fbm2 twice per pixel so this roughly halves its noise cost on mobile. No other look changes.
items.4_whiteout: solved -- musouFinisher()'s impact/flare bursts now scale their size (and, with a floor, alpha) by camera distance to the burst, referenced against ~10m (the far end of the finale's camera distances); at the leap/cut3 close framing (~2-3m) this meaningfully shrinks and dims them. Verified: 06-cleave-true-game-after.webp went from a near-total screen whiteout to a fully clean, readable shot (hero, enemies, HUD all visible); 05-leap-true-game-late-after.webp (captured right at/after impact) now shows a contained bright area (ground decal + a modest burst) rather than blowing out the whole frame.
items.5_split_resize: solved -- updateSplitShock() now checks the live canvas size every frame while the split is active and immediately ends the effect (hides the overlay) if it no longer matches the size the framebuffer was captured at, instead of rendering a stretched/misaligned frame for the rest of the split's (brief) duration.

round8.scope_note: Eighth pass (live user bug report, ece35a1). Files touched: combat-fx.js (fix + debugAftermath diagnostic), musou-v2.test.mjs (4 new tests). No battle.js/boot.js changes -- confirmed root cause is entirely inside combat-fx.js.
round8.root_cause: Two compounding bugs in the spirit-blade/flame-shroud state machine. (1) updateMusou()'s early-return when !musou.active never reached the updateSpirit() call at the bottom of the function -- the only place that force-hides those two meshes -- so once musou ended, whatever visible/opacity state they happened to be in froze forever. (2) updateSpirit()'s 'hidden'->'growing' trigger didn't check musou.impactT, so if the blade finished a full cleave->fade->hidden cycle while STILL inside the post-impact recovery window (musou.active not yet false), it immediately restarted growing, which the impactT>=0 block then forced straight back into 'cleaving' -- an infinite regrow loop that could get interrupted mid-cycle, mesh fully visible, the instant musou.active finally flipped false via bug (1).
round8.reproduction: Confirmed live via a new fx.debugAftermath() diagnostic polled through the real game (battle.js march level) at musouEnd +0.5/2/5/10s, both quality tiers, both forms. True-form runs reliably showed spiritBlade.visible=true, flameShroud.visible=true, spiritPhase stuck at 'cleaving' for the full 10s window (never reaching 'hidden'). Note: in the specific captured frames the frozen uOpacity/uReveal happened to be near-zero, so the screenshots don't show a dramatic white shape (confirmed via the 2 extra draw calls in the HUD's own draw counter instead: e.g. 102 vs 100 draws at +2s) -- the freeze point is effectively random per play session, so other sessions can freeze at a much more visible reveal/opacity, matching the live 'something white stays' report.
round8.fix: (a) updateMusou() now calls updateSpirit() from both the !musou.active early-return branch and the musou.endAt-triggered branch, so its internal safety-hide always runs the moment musou stops being active. (b) The 'hidden'->'growing' trigger now also requires musou.impactT < 0, so it can only fire before this musou's own finisher, never re-triggering after a cleave/fade cycle has already completed inside the same musou.
round8.tests: 4 new tests (desktop/mobile x std/true): after a full long musou + 3s of CHUNKY ~0.08s-step updates (fine 1/60 steps mostly missed the race window; the real game's slow-render frame times are what actually hit it), every cinematic mesh is hidden, spiritPhase is 'hidden', items/strip slots are drained, and fx.stats().drawCalls is exactly 0. Verified these tests fail against the pre-fix code (all 3 changes reverted) and pass with the fix restored.
round8.screenshots: 09-aftermath-{std,true}-game-{bug,fixed}-{2s,5s}.webp (plus 0.5s/10s bonus captures) in this directory, captured via the real march-level game.

round9.scope_note: Ninth pass (part 2 of the 'something white stays' report). Files touched: combat-fx.js, musou-v2.test.mjs. No battle.js/boot.js changes.
round9.root_cause: The finisher's ground crack/scorch/burst decals and dust/colour rings (from slam() and musouFinisher() directly) are strip-batch items whose aging used fxDt = max(gameDt, realDt*0.2) -- i.e. a floor of only 20% of real speed while ANY slow-mo track is active on the shared TimeScale singleton. The finisher's own slow-mo track normally clears quickly, but a nominal '1.6-1.8s life' decal aging at a fraction of real speed for even a brief window -- or, worse, for as long as other nearby hitstop-triggering hits keep re-arming the shared slow-mo (confirmed reproducible by injecting repeated hitstop events in a synthetic test) -- can take several real seconds to actually disappear, well past musouEnd.
round9.fix: Added a `musou` flag (reusing the existing per-item `.musou` semantics, previously only set on the rune decal) to decal()/groundRing()/pillar(), threaded through slam()'s own musou param (default false, so plunge/heavy/bossSlam callers of the same shared slam() function are completely unaffected) and set true only at musouFinisher()'s call site and its own direct groundRing/pillar calls. writeItems() now ages any `.musou` item on realDt directly instead of fxDt, so these items' fade is immune to slow-mo from any source, musou's own or otherwise. Combined with endMusou()'s existing 0.45s-forced-fade override (which now also lands in real seconds), the crack/scorch/burst/rings/pillar/rune are fully gone within ~1.6s of musouEnd, and the crack still reads bright for its first ~0.35-0.6s (natural fadeFrom) before fading.
round9.known_limitation: Finisher particles (STYLE.impact/flare/wisp/shard/rock/dust) share one GPU-instanced pool with a single global clock, so per-particle real-time aging isn't feasible without a larger redesign. Under normal (non-adversarial) conditions they finish well within 1.6s (confirmed in both the unit test and the real-game re-capture). Under a synthetic worst case with continuously re-armed nearby hitstops, a handful of small particles can outlive 1.6s -- but this doesn't match the user's reported symptom (a large ground shape), which is fully fixed.
round9.tests: Extended the round-8 aftermath tests (desktop/mobile x std/true) with an intermediate real-time checkpoint at musouEnd+1.6s: all strip/decal items gone and finisher particles dead. Verified this new assertion fails against the pre-fix code and passes with the fix restored (confirmed via a throwaway repro harness with injected hitstop events to force the adversarial slow-mo scenario, matching the mechanism believed responsible for the live report's multi-second persistence).
